purpose: Own the canonical names, identifiers, definitions, aliases, replacements, capitalization, and distinction rules used by the active kOA documentation corpus.

operation_verbs.meaning: Performs non-mutating access through a declared interface.
Admits content through a controlled authority boundary.
Produces an event, receipt, or declared output.
Makes a verified artifact or release current without partial authoritative state.
Creates candidate content that is not yet authoritative.
Converts validated candidate content into component-owned authoritative state.

distinction_rules.required_distinction: Resource control is separate from authorization, disclosure, consent, and governed privilege.
The Publication Gateway owns disclosure authorization; the UCKK Publication Bridge owns Moodle-specific packaging, transport, result handling, and receipts.
Local deterministic navigation is separate from the optional external voice capability.
The kOA Mediatheque and the UCKK Mediatheque use separate authority, storage, lifecycle, identity, access control, and operational ownership even when they use a compatible frame.
Runtime consumption is separate from language construction.
Execution of compiled language artifacts is separate from language build sessions.
A complete deployment identity is separate from a composable strengthening or restriction.
Architectural responsibility is separate from one running instance.
A deliverable is separate from the governed event that publishes it.
A compatible multi-channel version binding is separate from one independently versioned stream.
The complete isolation unit is separate from the Git checkout mechanism that may host it.
An unaccepted result is separate from component-owned accepted state.
Implementation guidance is separate from a testable active obligation.
Owner authorization is separate from the record of context, rationale, and consequences.
kOA Spaces composes presentation; Governance Policy Runtime owns applicable authorization, disclosure, consent, and governed privilege decisions.
A Space configures presentation for a context; a deployment profile defines system membership, resources, security, offline claims, and conformance.
An interface manifest contributes presentation metadata; a component or subsystem contract owns architecture, authority, behavior, and integration boundaries.

terms.definition: The optional approved external voice path used by Ariane without replacing local deterministic navigation.
An optional external capability accessed through an explicit user-triggered and capability-scoped boundary.
An AI capability shipped and executed as part of the kOA baseline.
A machine-readable policy governing cultural rights, consent, use, and disclosure conditions.
A machine-readable record of a governed decision and its relevant inputs, outcome, and authority.
A machine-readable declaration of an external integration, its capabilities, boundaries, and configuration.
A versioned package of compiled language artifacts.
A machine-readable declaration of a node's selected profile, overlays, capabilities, and constraints.
A verified package used to transfer approved artifacts into a disconnected environment.
A versioned package of governance policy artifacts.
A machine-readable record of artifact origin, processing, transfer, and acceptance history.
A machine-readable record of a publication decision and outcome.
A request submitted to the Publication Gateway for controlled cross-domain release.
A machine-readable declaration of CPU, memory, I/O, concurrency, queue, and process limits.
A versioned package consumed by a runtime component.
A package containing the artifacts and evidence required for a declared sovereign deployment operation.
A machine-readable allocation of host ports to one development workspace.
The release channel for governance policies and related authoritative bundles.
The release channel for Kristal, language, Atlas, runtime-pack, and approved knowledge artifacts.
The release channel for deployable application and component service artifacts.
The release channel for operating-system and system-image artifacts.

The host-local runtime boundary used when the independently owned Ariane ecosystem system is integrated into kOA-Linux. Ariane remains an integrated subsystem; this label does not transfer its internal domain or workflow authority to kOA-Linux.
The component that coordinates registered audit requests, evidence access, and selective disclosure.

Optional GF-focused language-development tooling used within SemantiK Architect workflows. GF is a renderer/backend and tooling source, not the architecture center of SemantiK Architect and not a separate ecosystem system.
The authority for authorization, disclosure, consent, governed privilege, and governed exceptions in profiles that deploy it.
The component authority for registered identity, trust-root, signature, and verification functions.

The internal kOA-Linux component that owns local media records, file versions, managed storage references, integrity state, collections, dimensions, rights, provenance, renditions, lifecycle, and local backup and restore state.
The node-local component that performs registered node management and reporting functions.

An independently owned ecosystem system for civic/public domain capabilities. kOA-Linux integrates it as a host-relative subsystem and does not own its internal model, workflow, API, or user interface.
The runtime that consumes and serves Kristal artifacts without becoming a universal operational database or workflow engine.
An independently owned ecosystem system for workflow and operational coordination. kOA-Linux integrates it as a host-relative subsystem and does not own its Task/Case/workflow internals.
The controlled boundary for cross-domain disclosure and publication.
The deterministic authority for CPU, memory, I/O, concurrency, queues, scheduling, and process limits.

The host-local runtime boundary used by kOA-Linux when SemantiK Architect is deployed. SemantiK Architect remains one independently owned planner-centered NLG ecosystem system; this runtime label does not redefine its internal planner, construction, lexicon, renderer, or API architecture.
An independently owned optional research and enrichment ecosystem subsystem whose output remains candidate data until explicitly reviewed and imported through a governed boundary.
Retired name from the former internal UCKK model. Active documentation uses either UCKK Publication Bridge for outbound publication or UCKK Import Bridge for inbound retrieval and quarantine.
Retired component identifier from the former internal UCKK model. It may appear only in migration or supersession material; active documentation uses UCKK for the external Moodle platform.
A permitted OCI-compatible container runtime for the Windows/WSL development profile.
A cluster orchestration platform permitted for selected hub, build-farm, or control-plane profiles and not required on endpoints.
An installed dependency environment whose contents can change during development and therefore cannot be shared between workspaces.
The preferred rootless container runtime for Linux development and sovereign Linux recipes.
The versioned Python project configuration file used by a workspace.
A systemd-oriented declarative mechanism used by applicable sovereign Linux recipes to manage Podman containers.
A container executed without host-root privileges.
A reusable download and build cache that may be shared because it does not represent a mutable installed environment.
The mandatory Python dependency and environment manager for kOA development workspaces.
The versioned UV dependency lock file used for reproducible synchronization.
A logical development isolation unit with its own identity, mutable dependencies, services, state, ports, secrets, and resource budget.
The stable identifier used to namespace mutable development resources.
The mutable Python virtual environment dedicated to one workspace.
A Git checkout mechanism that may host one workspace but does not itself define the complete workspace boundary.
The set of currently activated decisions, registries, contracts, ADRs, and normative documents.
The single current documentation tree under docs that participates in authority.
A record of architectural context, alternatives, rationale, consequences, and decision history.
A task-scoped generated projection that provides an AI agent with applicable authority, scope, requirements, locks, decisions, and prohibited assumptions.
Historical documentation retained without current product or documentation authority.
An immutable or versioned deliverable governed by an artifact class and lifecycle contract.
State accepted and owned by the component or registry responsible for the relevant domain.
The registry that activates the documentation release, registry versions, schema versions, authority order, ownership map, validation policy, and cutover state.
An external or generated result that has not yet been accepted into component-owned authoritative state.
The single machine-readable location authorized to define one architectural fact.
A repository-relative path, optionally followed by a JSON Pointer, that identifies an authoritative object.
A machine-readable registry with exclusive ownership of a defined architectural domain.

A first-class kOA-Linux architectural responsibility with explicit boundaries, owned state, interfaces, and failure behavior. An independently owned ecosystem system integrated by kOA-Linux remains an ecosystem system globally even when represented by a host-side subsystem boundary.
The rule that an operation requiring authority does not proceed when identity, policy, scope, compatibility, or ownership cannot be resolved.
A reproducible view of canonical data that carries no independent authority.
A versioned machine-readable assertion that prevents mutually dependent documentation objects from drifting out of alignment.
Read-only evidence that records source lineage, disposition, redirects, and cutover history without defining current product behavior.
A testable obligation with a stable requirement identifier, strength, scope, owner, source decision, and validation method.
The ability of declared core capabilities to remain available without Internet access within the applicable profile envelope.
An accepted decision that authorizes an implementation-affecting architectural fact or semantic change.
The ability to export, restore, migrate, and leave a deployment without dependence on an unavailable authority or proprietary-only path.
A complete deployable system identity that selects and constrains the global kOA baseline for a declared purpose.
A composable profile that strengthens or restricts a compatible primary profile without being independently deployable.
Non-normative implementation guidance that becomes binding only when explicitly adopted by an active profile contract.
A defined mechanism to challenge, review, correct, or reverse a governed decision or outcome.
A governed publication event that makes a versioned artifact or compatible artifact set available for activation.
An independently versioned stream of related artifact classes.
A signed or otherwise verified binding of compatible versions across the system, services, governance, and knowledge release channels.
Reduction of an affected capability without silently violating authority, integrity, or unrelated core behavior.
Accountability that exposes only the evidence required for the declared audit purpose.
One running deployment instance of a component or component capability.
An approved optional external integration surface named ChatGPT.
An approved optional external integration surface named Gamma.
An approved optional external integration surface named Suno.

The external online Moodle platform and UCKK Mediatheque. kOA-Linux may publish selected local content to it and import selected learning packages from it through separate governed directional integrations.

The controlled integration that packages and publishes explicitly authorized kOA content to UCKK, handles Moodle transport results, and preserves publication receipts without transferring local source authority.

The versioned portable interchange frame implemented by both the private offline kOA Mediatheque and the online UCKK Mediatheque for identity references, versions, integrity, media description, rights, provenance, lifecycle, mappings, packages, and receipts. Frame compatibility never merges authority, storage, identifiers, access control, or lifecycle.

The Mediatheque operated inside the external UCKK Moodle platform. It may use a frame compatible with the kOA Mediatheque while retaining separate authority, storage, lifecycle, identity, access control, and operational ownership.
A narrowly controlled emergency operation that requires explicit authorization, evidence, and post-event review.
The controlled admission of verified artifacts into a disconnected environment.
The kOA product family and umbrella name. In architecture text, use kOA Digital Ecosystem for the full system-of-systems scope and kOA-Linux Operating System for the local operating-system product.

The operable kOA system of systems: independently owned ecosystem systems, kOA-Linux platform capabilities, applications, gateways, artifacts, and explicit integration boundaries considered as one digital ecosystem.
An independently owned system in the kOA Digital Ecosystem with significant domain authority and boundaries that remain its own when hosted or integrated by kOA-Linux.

A host-relative classification used by kOA-Linux for an independently owned ecosystem system mounted or operated through a declared subsystem boundary. The classification does not transfer internal authority to kOA-Linux.
A bounded software or user-facing capability. An application can use or expose a domain without automatically becoming an independently owned ecosystem system.

A context-dependent convenience term. It is not a sufficient ownership category; normative architecture text qualifies the object as an ecosystem system, subsystem, component, application, service, runtime, gateway, or interface module.

The sovereign local operating system that provides execution, isolation, trust, storage, recovery, offline operation, resource governance, verified activation, and controlled integration for kOA ecosystem workloads.
Superseded former product name for kOA-Linux Operating System.
An overlay that constrains the user shell to a minimal appliance-oriented experience.
The reproducible build and artifact-production profile.
The profile for centralized coordination functions where those functions are explicitly deployed.
The native Linux development profile with isolated workspaces, UV-managed Python environments, and workspace-scoped services.
The Windows 11 and WSL2 development profile permitted for development convenience without sovereign Linux conformance.
An overlay that strengthens identity, verification, security, evidence, and operational controls.
A multi-service sovereign deployment profile for shared or coordinated operation.
The hardened Linux production profile with explicit identity, recovery, offline, privilege, and assurance controls.
An overlay that requires operation and recovery within a declared disconnected environment.
The lightweight end-user deployment profile for local daily operation on modest hardware.
A controlled release of information from one authority or security domain to another.
The governance domain that constrains use, disclosure, transformation, and publication according to registered cultural rights and consent.
A minimal broker that performs explicitly authorized host mutations without exposing general root access.
Evidence that proves a required property without indiscriminate disclosure of underlying private information.
A machine-readable inventory of software components and dependencies associated with an artifact or release.
A configured root of trust used to validate identity, signatures, or artifact provenance within a declared scope.

The controlled inbound integration that retrieves selected UCKK learning packages, places them in quarantine, validates source, license, integrity, provenance, and shared-frame compatibility, and presents them for explicit local acceptance.
The explicit outbound operation that obtains Publication Gateway authorization and sends a bounded selected representation to the online UCKK Mediatheque.
The explicit inbound operation that retrieves or receives a selected UCKK learning package, validates it in quarantine, and creates separate local kOA records only after acceptance.
A selected, complete, verifiable package of UCKK learning structure and shared-frame resources prepared for controlled local and offline use.
The optional, independently versioned, replaceable experience subsystem that composes navigation and interface contributions without owning business authority.
A user-facing arrangement that selects, orders, labels, and configures available interface modules for a declared context while preserving stable technical module identities.
The validated configuration artifact that identifies a Space, selects interface modules, applies public labels, defines ordering, and declares offline presentation behavior.
A module-owned manifest that contributes routes, sidebar entries, top-bar widgets, labels, capability requirements, and offline presentation behavior to kOA Spaces.
The upper-left control rendered by kOA Spaces for choosing among installed, activated, visible, and permitted interface modules.
A module-owned, validated navigation tree rendered in the left sidebar while that module is active.
A compact global or active-module contribution rendered in an approved top-bar slot as a shortcut, status indicator, or bounded action surface.
A three-state resilience policy that stops repeated calls to a failing dependency, fails fast while open, and admits bounded recovery probes.
The quarantined immutable record of asynchronous work that exhausted bounded retry or failed permanently and awaits governed closure.
An explicit multi-owner state machine using local transactions, idempotency, compensation, forward repair, and terminal evidence instead of a global lock.
A bounded verified reference to an owner-controlled object used instead of embedding a large payload in a general message or event.
A presentation-owned adapter that shapes and aggregates owner queries for one experience without acquiring business authority.
A non-authoritative command-free read model rebuilt from a declared authoritative source with explicit lag and deletion propagation.
A versioned cache-aside policy defining source ownership, keys, TTL, invalidation, staleness, security, failure behavior, and metrics.
